passage: I am Sabina, and this is about the form I backdated. Wasim, my manager, came to my desk on a Friday. "Just put last Monday's date on the safety checklist. The inspection is Tuesday, and it was done anyway, more or less." Two colleagues were within earshot, and one looked up and then down at a screen. I said "Okay" before my brain caught up. I told myself it was his call and he was the one signing. I typed the old date, and my hands felt oddly cold. That night I realised nobody had forced me. I had simply been handed a way not to decide.

qa.q: Which date did Sabina type on the safety checklist?
qa.a: Sabina typed last Monday's date on the safety checklist.

qa.q: Why did Sabina say "Okay" before thinking it through?
qa.a: Sabina felt the decision belonged to Wasim, which brought a brief relief; the cold hands suggest an uneasy sense that this was not really acceptable.

qa.q: What could Sabina have done at the desk instead of saying "Okay"?
qa.a: Sabina could have asked "is this okay?", asked for the request in writing, or taken the question to the proper channel, since following a request does not remove personal responsibility.

qa.q: How might the colleague who looked up and then down have been feeling?
qa.a: That colleague may have felt uncomfortable but unwilling to step in, assuming, like Sabina, that it was not their decision to make.

grounding: An employee complies with a manager's request to backdate a form, telling themselves it is not their decision, with responsibility diffused.

passage: Compliance note, Thursday. Samir, a junior engineer, changed two readings in the site report after his manager Vidya said, "Smooth it, the client is nervous." In the corridor Samir told me, "It was not my decision," and looked relieved and sick at the same time. The two others on the team said they knew but had not thought it was theirs to raise. I told Samir that a request from a manager does not remove personal responsibility and that he can ask for it in writing. The same day I raised the report with the head of quality, who has asked for the original readings to be restored. — Naveen, compliance officer

qa.a: Naveen told Samir personal responsibility remains and to ask for such requests in writing, and raised the report with the head of quality the same day so the readings could be restored.

subtype: Following a boss into a grey area [Actor]
passage:
Sit, Nilesh. You asked how I became so fussy about paperwork. I'm Lokesh, your old senior, and I'll tell you.
When I was your age, at the textile mill, my boss handed me a machine inspection form on a Friday. “Put last month's date on it. The inspector is coming Monday. It's a formality.”
The whole shift knew. Nobody said anything. I told myself: I only hold the pen, the decision is his. I signed.
Three weeks later that loom jammed and a young helper's hand was hurt. Not badly, thank God. But I remember sitting in the canteen, staring at my own signature on that form.
Every one of us had thought, not my decision. That's how it happened.

qa.q: What date was young Lokesh asked to put on the form?
qa.a: Young Lokesh was asked to put last month's date on it.

qa.q: How did young Lokesh feel staring at his signature?
qa.a: Lokesh felt guilty and shaken, knowing that the signature had helped hide an unchecked machine.

qa.q: At what moment in the story could Lokesh have made a different choice?
qa.a: When the boss handed over the form, Lokesh could have asked for the inspection to be done first or refused to sign a false date.

qa.q: How might the young helper see what happened?
qa.a: The helper probably felt frightened and let down, since everyone above had signed off on a machine nobody checked.

grounding: An elder recalls backdating a form for a boss, reasoning that it wasn't the elder's decision, and how shared silence led to harm.

passage:
The school office had no power, the inverter was dead, and the district inspection team was due at ten. Principal Aditi Rao paced beside Lakshmi's desk.
“The parent-teacher meeting register for July. We never got signatures. Just fill in the dates and ask the peons to sign as parents.”
Lakshmi's pen hovered. Through the window she could see two teachers watching, then looking away.
“Ma'am, the parents didn't—”
“Lakshmi, it's paperwork. I take responsibility.”
The clock said nine-twenty. Lakshmi filled in the dates. When the inspector later flipped through the register and nodded, she felt her face go hot. At lunch she couldn't eat. It was ma'am's decision, she kept telling herself. It didn't help.

qa.q: Who did the principal ask to sign as parents?
qa.a: She asked the peons to sign as parents.

qa.q: What was Lakshmi feeling when the inspector nodded?
qa.a: She felt ashamed and anxious; her face went hot and she couldn't eat, even while telling herself it was ma'am's decision.

qa.q: What could Lakshmi have said when her pen hovered?
qa.a: She could have calmly said she wasn't comfortable signing false entries and suggested telling the inspector the meeting records were incomplete.

qa.q: How might the two teachers at the window feel about what they saw?
qa.a: They looked away, so they may feel uneasy and relieved it wasn't them, sharing the silence that let it happen.

grounding: Shows an employee backdating a register under time pressure because her boss asks, telling herself it isn't her decision.

subtype: Following a boss into a grey area [Actor]
passage:
On the last working day of the month, Hrithik called Sunaina into his glass cabin at the logistics office in Andheri.
“The client report. Three late deliveries. Mark them on time. The trucks were only a day behind, na?”
Sunaina glanced through the glass. Pradeep and Farah were at their desks, heads down. Everyone in the team knew the numbers were going to be smoothed. Nobody had said a word last month either.
“Okay, sir,” she said.
Back at her desk she changed the three dates. It isn't my decision, she thought. I'm just updating a sheet. She clicked send.
On the way home in the local train, she realised she wouldn't have done it on her own. Not in a hundred years.

qa.q: How many late deliveries were in the client report?
qa.a: There were three late deliveries.

qa.q: What was Sunaina thinking as she changed the dates?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and tried to calm herself by thinking it wasn't her decision and she was only updating a sheet.

qa.q: What might help Sunaina next month?
qa.a: She could ask Hrithik to put the instruction in writing or talk to Pradeep and Farah about raising it together, instead of going along alone.

qa.q: How might the client be affected by the smoothed report?
qa.a: The client gets a false picture of delivery times and can't plan or complain fairly, which could hurt them later.

grounding: Shows an employee who smooths a report at her boss's request, telling herself it is not her decision, something she would never choose alone.

passage:
"Vikas, the approval form for the new vendor. Put the date as the twelfth."
"Today's the nineteenth, Himani."
"I know. The audit window closed on the fifteenth. It's just paperwork. Before lunch, please."
Her door clicked shut. Arun leaned over from the next desk. "The twelfth?"
"She said so."
"Your name goes in the 'prepared by' box, though."
"It's her call. She's the manager. If audit asks, I'll say she told me."
"And you think that'll help?"
Vikas opened the form. The cursor blinked in the date field. "Everyone does this. Deepa did it last quarter."
"Deepa also cried in the stairwell when audit called her in."
Vikas typed 1 and 2, deleted them, then typed them again. "It's not my decision," he said, mostly to the screen.

qa.q: What date did Himani ask Vikas to put on the form?
qa.a: The twelfth.

qa.q: What does Vikas saying "It's not my decision" mostly to the screen suggest?
qa.a: Vikas feels uneasy and guilty, and repeats the line to quiet his own doubt rather than because he believes it.

qa.q: What could Vikas do instead of typing the date?
qa.a: He could ask Himani to put the instruction in writing or raise it through a proper channel, and decline to sign a date he knows is wrong.

qa.q: How does Arun see Vikas's choice?
qa.a: Arun seems worried for Vikas, reminding him that his own name goes on the form whatever Himani ordered.

grounding: Illustrates an employee asked to backdate a form who complies while telling himself it is not his decision.
